title: Abdul El-Sayed Wins Michigan Senate Race, Defeating Mike Rogers; Would Be First Muslim Senator
dek: The progressive Democrat won an open seat that was pivotal to the fight for Senate control, according to AP, The Washington Post and NBC News.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: The U.S. Capitol, west front (file photo)

keyPoints: AP reported that Democrat Abdul El-Sayed defeated Republican Mike Rogers for Michigan's open Senate seat, a race AP described as pivotal in the fight for control of the chamber.
The Washington Post reported that El-Sayed would be the first Muslim elected to the Senate.
NBC News described El-Sayed as an epidemiologist and former public health official aligned with the Democratic Party's left flank.
The Guardian reported that El-Sayed, 42, declared victory early Wednesday at the state Democratic headquarters in Detroit.
body:
Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won Michigan's U.S. Senate race on Tuesday, defeating Republican former Rep. Mike Rogers for the open seat, according to reporting from the Associated Press, The Washington Post, NBC News and The Guardian.

## The result

AP reported that El-Sayed, a progressive, defeated Rogers for an open seat that was pivotal in the fight for control of the Senate. The Washington Post reported that El-Sayed ran on promises to disrupt how Washington does business, and that he would become the first Muslim elected to the Senate.

The Guardian reported that El-Sayed, 42, declared victory early Wednesday at the state Democratic Party headquarters in Detroit. NBC News described him as an epidemiologist and former public health official aligned with the party's left flank.

## Context

AP's reporting on the wider midterms says Democrats won control of the Senate and held Michigan. El-Sayed's win keeps that seat in Democratic hands.

An Al Jazeera preview published Nov. 1 described Trump and El-Sayed both campaigning in Michigan in the final days before the vote. A CBS News weekend live blog reported that a Democratic rift in Michigan had become public during the final push. The reporting reviewed for this story does not describe the substance of that rift, so this story does not characterize it.

## Senate context

AP reported that Democrats won control of the Senate on Tuesday night, flipping at least seven seats held by Republicans, including Kansas, Iowa, Texas, Ohio, Maine, North Carolina and South Carolina. Democrats also held Georgia and Michigan. AP described the overall outcome as a rebuke of Republican governance in Washington.

Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer called the results a 'generational remake of the Senate map,' according to AP. The Hill reported that Schumer is expected to be elected majority leader when Senate Democrats hold leadership elections in early December. Senate Majority Leader John Thune, a Republican, said on X that Senate Republicans 'will not stand idly by.'

## What is not yet known

The reporting reviewed for this story does not include a final certified vote margin. Meridian will update this story if official totals change the result.
